about: A labelled corpus for the deterministic half of Nexus understanding.
Each case is a room window plus the anchor message a pass would be about,
and the reading the server should reach. The harness in tools/eval_intent.py
scores it; tests/test_intent_eval.py holds the floor.
expect.expression_kind  the deictic kind the resolver should find ('' for none)
expect.referent         the Telegram id the message points at, or null
expect.requires_resolution  whether the text alone leaves the referent open
expect.ambiguous        whether the server should report it could not tell
expect.addressed        whether addressing.addressed should fire
A note on `ambiguous` and an empty room: with no window there is nothing to
be ambiguous *between*, so the flag is false and the render says the server
found no candidate. That is a different reading from 'these two are too
close', and the corpus keeps them distinct on purpose.
expect.when             the time word's direction ('', past, now, future, repeat)
expect.when_unit        its granularity ('' or minute/hour/day/week/month/year)
expect.when is '' for a message with no time word, and a claimed reading
there is a false positive: the server would be placing a time nobody stated.
expect.state            the room-state reading:
.edges                the reply edges [[source_id, target_id]], oldest first
.focus                the target the replies converge on (0 when none)
.relation             '' / continues / shifts / unclear — scored only where
labelled, because it is a reading rather than a record

cases.note: A reply to رضا and «اینو» — the id is the answer, not a candidate.
Colloquial object form: the clitic is reported, because it is checked with the explicit person-words before any bare demonstrative.
«این کاربر» as a reply — person kind, and the edge still settles it.
No demonstrative at all: the object is the clitic on the verb.
«بنش کن» with one person having just spoken.
No reply edge, but the instruction names رضا.
The instruction states the Telegram id outright.
«ادمینه» with exactly one administrator in the room.
«ادمینه» with two administrators is not a referent — ask.
A member spoke more recently, but «ادمینه» is the administrator.
«همون کاربر» — three replies in a row aimed at رضا.
«ساکتش کن» — the clitic «ـش» is a pronoun, and the room has been replying to رضا.
«همون کاربر», but the room's replies are split between رضا and سارا — the anaphor does not settle it.
Three people spoke moments ago and nobody was replied to — do not guess.
One person spoke just before; still not a confident referent alone.
«قبلیش» points backwards; the kind is recorded even when weak.
Persian and English in one sentence: «این user».
A Latin role word with a Persian instruction.
Fully English phrasing with a Persian room.
Ordinary conversation points at nobody.
An explicit name needs no resolution — the transcript already carries it.
A price question is not a person reference.
A word ending in «و» must not be read as a demonstrative.
A bare action stem has no object; only the clitic does.
Nexus called by name, with an instruction.
The name written the way a group writes it.
The object marker attached to the name, and a clitic on the verb.
A quotation about Nexus is a mention, not a call: the name is the subject of a reporting verb.

anchor.name: رضا
anchor.text: نکسوس گفت که اینو بن کنه

cases.note: A quotation about Nexus is a mention, not a call: the name is the subject of a reporting verb.
Talking about Nexus mid-sentence. KNOWN GAP, left on purpose: every deterministic rule that catches it also demotes a real request.
A member addressing Nexus is addressed, even though they cannot act.
A misspelled instruction still carries its deictic.
A zero-width non-joiner inside the phrase must not split it.
Arabic yeh/kaf folded to Persian before matching.
A correction that names the person it corrects to.

anchor.name: مالک
anchor.text: نه منظورم مهدی بود، اینو بن کن

cases.note: A sudden unrelated message carries no person reference.
A temporal word is not a person reference.

anchor.name: مالک
anchor.text: قبلاً گفتم که اینکار رو نکنید

cases.note: A chain of replies between two people; the edge names the target.
The owner's instruction with a reply edge is the confident case.
An administrator's instruction behaves the same as the owner's.
Slang for muting, with a reply edge.
A plain question with a question mark.
Colloquial «چخبر؟» — a question with no question word.
A greeting, not an instruction.
Reporting what somebody else said — not an order to Nexus.
A correction with no question and no directive.
An ordinary imperative whose verb is in no lexicon; «کن» carries it.
A Persian/English directive.
A follow-up directive built on «بده».
IMPLICIT INTENT, left as a known gap: a complaint that asks for nothing in words. No deterministic marker fires, and inventing one would fire on every complaint in the room.

anchor.name: مالک
anchor.text: یکی اینجا خیلی داره شلوغ میکنه

cases.note: An ordinary statement. The server abstains rather than guess.
A polite request phrased as a question. Read as a question, because the mark is the marker that decides and second-guessing it needs semantics — recorded as a boundary, not a bug.
A question with a reply pointing at it is not open.
A question nothing replies to stays open.
Two questions, one answered: only the unanswered one is reported.
«همین الان» is the present moment, read from the server's clock.
«چند دقیقه پیش» points back at a scale of minutes and states no count.
«امروز» is the present, at a scale of days.
«فردا» points forwards, at a scale of days.
A question whose time word points back a day.
«اون موقع» points back at a time the room established; no scale stated.
«هنوز» is about the present state — "still has not".
«دوباره» says this has happened before; a direction the words state.
No time word at all: the reading is empty, not wrong.
«هفته پیش» points back a week.
A time word in a Persian/English mixed sentence.
A colloquial question whose time word is «دیشب».
«فردا اون موقع» is the future: the word that states a direction decides.
«همین‌الان» with the ZWNJ is the same present moment.
«چند وقت پیش» is "a while ago": a direction and no scale.
«چند ساعت پیش» is a duration, not a question — the noun after «چند» decides.
Two people reply to the same person: that is a convergence, and the anchor continues the file thread.
One reply edge is reported but is not called a convergence.
No reply edges at all, and the anchor still continues the thread.
A substantive message that shares no content word: a change of subject.
A shared noun is the evidence, and it is reported.
Replies split between two people: the focus is the more recent, and the short anchor is not judged.
The anchor's own reply edge is in the graph even with no window, and there is nothing before it to continue.
Two shared content words, both reported.
A two-word message shares nothing with anything and is not judged.
A reply chain, and the anchor continues the thread it belongs to.
A graph is present and the anchor still changes the subject.
